title: San Francisco’s pension fund beside other California local funds
question: Is San Francisco’s pension fund better or worse funded than the funds of comparable California cities and counties?
finding: In the State Controller’s table for fiscal 2024, San Francisco’s fund reports 96.6% of its promises funded (valuation of 2023-07-01), rank 6 of the 17 local funds pulled; the middle fund reports 88.0%. San Francisco’s share was 86.3% in the fiscal 2017 table. The lowest is Golden Gate Transit District Amalgamated Retirement Plan at 48.0%.
how: State Controller “Funding Position” table for retirement systems, fiscal 2017 to 2024: the funded share each system reports on its own smoothed asset value, and on market value where given. The systems are those of the comparison cities and counties that run their own fund, plus two Bay Area transit district plans.
limits: Each fund sets its own assumed return, wage growth and life expectancy, so funded shares are not measured on one yardstick; a fund with a more cautious assumption looks worse funded. Valuation dates differ by up to a year between funds and the table can lag (San Francisco’s row uses a valuation a year older than the fiscal year). Long Beach and Santa Clara County belong to the statewide public employees’ fund and have no row of their own. Small plans can sit far above or below 100% for reasons unrelated to how well they are run. The dollar columns of this table are not used: Alameda County Employees' Retirement Association; City of Oakland Fire and Police Retirement System; San Francisco City and County Employees' Retirement System report some years in thousands and others in dollars, which looks like a filing error in the source.
